easy.def: To make or finish something.
examples: I do my homework at night.
She did a good job.
Dad is doing the dishes.

more.def: To carry out an action, finish a task, or take part in something.
examples: Please do your chores before you go out to play.
The scientists did an experiment with magnets.
We have done all the puzzles in this book.

easy.def: A short name for a doctor.
examples: The doc looked in my ears.
Doc, my arm hurts.
I asked the doc a question.

more.def: An informal, short name for a doctor.
examples: The doc said I should rest.
Ask the doc if you can swim.
Everyone in town calls her Doc.

easy.def: A place where boats stop and are tied up.
examples: The boat is at the dock.
We stood on the dock.
The dock is wooden.

more.def: A platform by the water where boats stop and are tied up.
examples: The boat bumped gently against the dock.
We fished off the dock.
The sailors tied the ship to the dock.

easy.def: A person who helps sick people feel better.
examples: The doctor looked at my ear.
My mom is a doctor.
We saw the doctor.

more.def: A person who is trained to treat people who are sick or hurt.
examples: The doctor listened to my heart with a stethoscope.
My aunt is a doctor at the children's hospital.
We visit the doctor once a year for a checkup.

easy.def: A paper with important writing on it.
examples: The teacher read the document.
Dad signed the document.
This document has my name.

more.def: A piece of writing that gives facts or has important information on it.
examples: Dad signed the document at the bank.
The passport is an important document.
I saved the document on the computer.

easy.def: A movie or show about real things.
examples: We watched a documentary.
The documentary is about whales.
A documentary shows facts.

more.def: A movie or television program that gives facts about real people, places or events.
examples: We watched a documentary about whales in science class.
The documentary showed how bees make honey.
She made a documentary about her town's history.

easy.def: A person who moves quickly to get out of the way.
examples: The dodger ducked.
A dodger moves fast.
He is a quick dodger.

more.def: A person who moves quickly to avoid something.
examples: The dodger ducked and the ball missed him.
A good dodger wins at dodgeball.
He is such a quick dodger that no one can hit him.

easy.def: An animal people keep as a pet that barks.
examples: My dog runs fast.
The dog barked.
We walk the dog.

more.def: A furry animal that is kept as a pet or used for work, such as guarding or herding.
examples: Our dog loves to chase a ball in the park.
The sheepdog herded the sheep into the barn.
A guide dog helps a person who cannot see.

easy.def: A word for a dog that little children use.
examples: The doggy barked.
I see the doggy.
The doggy is soft.

more.def: A friendly word for a dog, often used with young children.
examples: The little boy waved at the doggy.
Look at the cute doggy!
The doggy wagged its tail.

easy.def: A toy shaped like a person.
examples: She plays with a doll.
The doll has a dress.
I got a new doll.

more.def: A toy that looks like a small person or baby.
examples: She dressed her doll in a tiny coat.
The doll had soft yellow hair.
He sewed a doll for his sister.

easy.def: Money worth 100 cents.
examples: The apple costs one dollar.
I have five dollars.
She saved a dollar.

more.def: A unit of money in the United States and some other countries, equal to 100 cents.
examples: A dollar is made up of one hundred cents.
The lemonade cost two dollars.
He saved every dollar for a new bike.

easy.def: A smart sea animal that jumps.
examples: The dolphin jumped.
A dolphin swims fast.
We saw a dolphin.

more.def: A smart sea animal with a long snout that breathes air and is known for jumping.
examples: The dolphin leaped out of the water.
Dolphins talk to each other with clicks.
A dolphin followed our boat.

easy.def: A round roof like half a ball.
examples: The building has a dome.
A dome is round.
The dome was gold.

more.def: A round roof that is shaped like half of a ball, or any rounded shape like it.
examples: The old church has a giant dome that can be seen from far away.
The planetarium's dome is the screen for the stars.
A glass dome covered the cake.

easy.def: Having to do with the home.
examples: Dogs are domestic animals.
The domestic cat is a pet.
She does domestic chores.

more.def: Having to do with the home or family, or tamed to live with people.
examples: Dogs and cats are domestic animals.
She does domestic chores like cooking.
We took a domestic flight within our country.

easy.def: To train an animal to live with people.
examples: People domesticated the dog.
They domesticated sheep.
Cats were domesticated long ago.

more.def: To tame an animal or grow a plant so that it can live with people or be used by them.
examples: People domesticated wolves thousands of years ago, and those wolves became dogs.
Farmers domesticated wild plants to grow as crops.
It took many years to domesticate the horse.

easy.def: The strongest or most important.
examples: The lion is the dominant animal.
The dominant color is blue.
A dominant leader.

more.def: Stronger or more important than the others in a group.
examples: The dominant wolf leads the pack.
Blue is the dominant color in the painting.
The team was dominant all season and won every game.

easy.def: To be the strongest or most important.
examples: Our team dominates the game.
The tall tree dominates the yard.
The big dog dominated the pack.

more.def: To have more power or control than others, or to be the most noticeable.
examples: Our team dominated the game and scored six goals.
The tall mountain dominates the view from our window.
One loud voice dominated the talk until the teacher asked for others to speak.

easy.def: A small flat piece with dots, used in a game.
examples: I stood a domino up.
A domino fell.
We play with dominoes.

more.def: A small, flat, rectangular tile marked with dots, used in a game.
examples: I stood a domino on its end and pushed it over.
She lined up the dominoes in a long, winding row.
A domino game needs lots of tiles with dots on them.

easy.def: To give something to help others.
examples: I donate my old toys.
She donated her coat.
We donated money.

more.def: To give money or things to help a person or group.
examples: I donated my old toys to the shelter.
She donated her coat to the clothing drive.
We donated food to the pantry.

easy.def: A gift of money or things.
examples: We made a donation.
The donation was food.
The donation helped.

more.def: Something such as money or food that is given to help others.
examples: We made a donation to the food bank.
The donation was a box of toys.
Many donations came in.

easy.def: An animal like a small horse with long ears.
examples: The donkey carried a load.
A donkey says hee-haw.
We rode a donkey.

more.def: An animal like a small horse that has long ears and a loud bray.
examples: The donkey carried baskets up the hill.
A donkey brays loudly.
We rode a donkey at the farm.

easy.def: A person who gives something to help.
examples: The donor gave money.
A blood donor helps others.
The donors were thanked.

more.def: A person who gives money, blood or something else to help others.
examples: The donor gave money to the library.
A blood donor can save lives.
The school thanked its donors.

easy.def: To draw without thinking much.
examples: I doodle on my paper.
She doodled a cat.
He doodled during class.

more.def: To draw little pictures or shapes while you are thinking about something else.
examples: I doodle on my paper while I listen.
She doodled a cat in the margin.
He doodled stars during the long meeting.

easy.def: A quick, messy drawing.
examples: I made a doodle.
The doodle is funny.
A doodle of a cat.

more.def: A quick drawing made without much thought.
examples: I made a doodle on my notebook.
The doodle looked like a funny dog.
She added a doodle to the corner of the page.

easy.def: A terrible end that cannot be avoided.
examples: The doom of the ship was near.
Doom awaited them.
The old story is full of doom.

more.def: A very bad fate or end that seems sure to come.
examples: The sailors knew their doom was near.
The villain's doom came at the end of the story.
A sense of doom filled the dark room.

easy.def: A part you open to go in or out.
examples: Close the door.
Knock on the door.
The door is red.

more.def: A part of a building, room, or car that opens and closes so people can go in or out.
examples: She knocked on the door and waited for an answer.
The door to the classroom opens into the hallway.
Please shut the car door gently.

easy.def: A button that makes a sound when someone is at the door.
examples: I rang the doorbell.
The doorbell rang.
The doorbell is loud.

more.def: A button by a door that makes a ringing sound when you press it.
examples: I rang the doorbell and waited.
The doorbell rang while we ate dinner.
The dog barked at the doorbell.

easy.def: The round handle you turn to open a door.
examples: I turned the doorknob.
The doorknob is shiny.
Hang it on the doorknob.

more.def: The round handle on a door that you turn to open or close it.
examples: I turned the doorknob and pushed open the door.
A sign hung on the doorknob that said "Do not disturb."
The brass doorknob was cold to the touch.

easy.def: A person whose job is to open the door at a building.
examples: The doorman said hello.
The doorman opened the door.
A doorman is at the hotel.

more.def: A person whose job is to open the door and help visitors at a hotel or large building.
examples: The doorman said hello and opened the door.
A doorman in a red coat stood at the hotel.
The doorman called us a taxi.

easy.def: The step in front of a door.
examples: The cat sat on the doorstep.
A box was on the doorstep.
We waited on the doorstep.

more.def: The step or small platform just outside a door.
examples: The cat sat on the doorstep and waited.
A package was left on the doorstep.
We waited on the doorstep until Mom came.

easy.def: The opening where a door is.
examples: She stood in the doorway.
The cat sat in the doorway.
He walked through the doorway.

more.def: The opening in a wall that you walk through, where a door is.
examples: She stood in the doorway and waved goodbye.
The cat sat in the sunny doorway all afternoon.
A big box was too wide to fit through the doorway.

easy.def: Silly or slow to understand.
examples: The dopey dog fell over.
He made a dopey face.
That was a dopey thing to do.

more.def: Silly, or not quick to notice or understand things.
examples: The dopey puppy tripped over its own paws.
He wore a dopey grin and a funny hat.
I felt dopey after waking from a long nap.

easy.def: A building where students sleep at school.
examples: The students live in a dorm.
The dorm has rooms.
My cousin lives in a dorm.

more.def: A short word for dormitory, a building where students live at a school or college.
examples: My cousin lives in a dorm at college.
The dorm has a big common room.
Students dropped their bags in the dorm.

easy.def: A building where students live.
examples: The students live in a dormitory.
The dormitory has many rooms.
My cousin lives in a dormitory.

more.def: A building at a school or college with rooms where students sleep.
examples: The dormitory was quiet during exams.
The dormitory has a big common room.
She unpacked her bags in the dormitory.

easy.def: How much medicine to take.
examples: The dosage is on the bottle.
Ask for the right dosage.
The dosage is small.

more.def: The amount of medicine that a person should take at one time, and how often.
examples: The doctor told us the right dosage for the medicine.
The dosage is printed on the bottle.
Never take more than the dosage that your doctor says.

easy.def: An amount of medicine.
examples: Take one dose.
The dose is small.
She took her dose.

more.def: A measured amount of medicine that you take at one time.
examples: The nurse measured the dose of medicine.
Take one dose every morning.
The dose for children is smaller.

easy.def: A tiny round spot.
examples: I drew a dot.
The shirt has dots.
The dot is red.

more.def: A small round mark or spot.
examples: I drew a dot on the paper.
The ladybug has black dots.
Connect the dots to see the picture.

easy.def: Two times as much.
examples: I got a double scoop.
Use double the flour.
A double bed fits two.

more.def: Twice as much or twice as many.
examples: She ordered a double scoop of ice cream.
The recipe needs double the amount of flour.
A double window keeps out the cold.

easy.def: To make two times as much.
examples: Double the recipe.
The plant doubled in size.
The money doubled.

more.def: To make something twice as big or twice as many.
examples: We doubled the recipe to feed the whole class.
The plant doubled in height in a week.
Sales doubled this year.

easy.def: To not be sure.
examples: I doubt it will rain.
She doubts he is right.
I doubt she knows.

more.def: To think that something is probably not true.
examples: I doubt that it will snow today.
She doubted that the story was true.
He doubts he can lift the box.

easy.def: A feeling of not being sure.
examples: I have some doubt.
There is no doubt.
Doubt made him stop.

more.def: A feeling of not being sure about something.
examples: There was no doubt that it was her coat.
A little doubt crossed his mind.
She had doubts about the plan.

easy.def: Not sure that something will happen.
examples: It is doubtful.
I feel doubtful.
A doubtful look.

more.def: Not sure about something, or not likely to be true or to happen.
examples: It is doubtful that the game will go ahead in this rain.
She gave a doubtful look when I said I had seen a unicorn.
I was doubtful about the new idea.

easy.def: A soft, thick mix of flour and water that you bake.
examples: Mom made bread dough.
The dough is soft.
We rolled the dough.

more.def: A thick, soft mixture of flour, water and other things that is baked into bread or cookies.
examples: Mom rolled the dough for the pie.
The cookie dough was sticky.
We let the dough rise.

easy.def: A ring of sweet fried dough.
examples: I ate a doughnut.
The doughnut has sprinkles.
The doughnut is sweet.

more.def: A round, sweet treat made of fried dough, often with a hole in the middle.
examples: I had a doughnut with sprinkles.
The bakery sells fresh doughnuts.
She dunked her doughnut in milk.

easy.def: A white or gray bird that stands for peace.
examples: The dove is white.
A dove coos.
The dove flew away.

more.def: A gentle bird with soft feathers that is a symbol of peace.
examples: A white dove flew up from the tree.
Doves make a soft, cooing sound.
The dove is a symbol of peace.

easy.def: Toward a lower place.
examples: The ball rolled down.
Sit down, please.
The sun goes down.

more.def: Toward a lower place or position, or from a higher one to a lower one.
examples: The leaves floated down from the tree and landed on the pond.
Please sit down and open your books.
We walked down the hill to the river.

easy.def: Toward the bottom of a hill.
examples: The ball rolled downhill.
We ran downhill.
The sled went downhill.

more.def: Toward the bottom of a slope or hill.
examples: The sled raced downhill and came to a stop at the bottom.
The stream flows downhill into the lake.
She rode her bike downhill with the wind in her face.

easy.def: Going down a hill.
examples: It is a downhill run.
The downhill path is easy.
A downhill race.

more.def: Sloping downward, or going toward the bottom of a hill.
examples: The downhill path was easy, so we reached the bottom quickly.
He won the downhill ski race.
After the long climb, the downhill walk felt easy.

easy.def: To or on a lower floor.
examples: Go downstairs.
The kitchen is downstairs.
I ran downstairs.

more.def: To or on a lower floor of a building.
examples: Our laundry room is downstairs.
Dad carried the laundry downstairs.
Meet me downstairs in five minutes.

easy.def: The busy middle part of a city.
examples: We went downtown.
The stores are downtown.
The library is downtown.

more.def: The central part of a city or town, where many stores and offices are.
examples: We took the bus downtown to see the parade.
Tall buildings crowd downtown.
The museum is in downtown near the river.

easy.def: To sleep lightly for a short time.
examples: Grandpa dozed in his chair.
The cat dozed in the sun.
I dozed on the couch.

more.def: To sleep lightly for a short time, usually when you did not mean to.
examples: Grandpa dozed in his chair after lunch.
The cat dozed in a patch of sunlight.
I dozed off during the long car ride.

easy.def: A group of twelve.
examples: A dozen eggs.
I bought a dozen donuts.
There are a dozen kids.

more.def: A group of twelve things.
examples: Mom bought a dozen eggs.
A dozen roses stood in the vase.
There are a dozen months in a year.
